microtheory.name: cerebellar_circuit
microtheory.definition: The cerebellum's canonical microcircuit — Marr 1969, Albus 1971, Ito's revisions. The cerebellum has more neurons than the rest of the brain combined (80%); maps not to motor cortex but to ALL cortical regions via cerebro-cerebellar loops. Modern view: the cerebellum is a universal predictor — supplies expectation-of-consequence to whatever it's connected to. Substrate analogue: the anticipation handler (∂²F prediction).

concepts.name: purkinje_cell
concepts.definition: The cerebellum's only output neuron. Massive fan-shaped dendritic arbor receives ~150,000 parallel-fiber synapses. Inhibits deep cerebellar nuclei. Substrate analogue: the output aggregator of an anticipation Mt.

concepts.name: granule_cell
concepts.definition: Smallest, most numerous neurons in the brain (~50 billion in human cerebellum). Receive mossy fiber input; their axons form parallel fibers. Expand mossy fiber input into a high-dimensional sparse code (Marr 1969). Substrate analogue: sparse expansion concepts for feature recombination.

concepts.name: mossy_fiber
concepts.definition: Cerebellar input from pons (carrying cortical info) + spinal cord. Multiple firing modes. Encodes context for prediction. Substrate analogue: context-input edges feeding the anticipation Mt.

concepts.name: climbing_fiber
concepts.definition: Cerebellar input from inferior olive. Each Purkinje cell receives just ONE climbing fiber, but it makes hundreds of synapses. Fires sparsely (~1 Hz) but with massive effect — encodes the error signal. Substrate analogue: ΔF teaching signal for the anticipation Mt.

concepts.name: parallel_fiber
concepts.definition: Granule cell axon. Bifurcates + runs longitudinally for several mm, contacting many Purkinje cells in a row. Conveys context to multiple predictors. Substrate analogue: shared context concept reachable by many anticipation handlers.

concepts.name: inferior_olive
concepts.definition: Brainstem nucleus, source of climbing fibers. Computes prediction-error from comparison of intended vs actual movement / outcome. Substrate analogue: ΔF computation in _stash_post_state.

concepts.name: deep_cerebellar_nuclei
concepts.definition: Cerebellum's actual output. Receive inhibition from Purkinje cells + excitation from collaterals. Send predictions back to cortex via thalamus. Substrate analogue: anticipation output that propagates to other Mts.

concepts.name: cerebellar_long_term_depression
concepts.definition: Cerebellar LTD. Coincident climbing-fiber + parallel-fiber input WEAKENS the parallel-fiber-Purkinje synapse. Opposite sign from cortical LTP. The Marr-Albus learning rule. Substrate analogue: prediction-error-driven weight DECAY in the anticipation Mt's connections.

concepts.name: marr_albus_model
concepts.definition: 1969-1971 theory: granule cells expand mossy-fiber input into a high-dimensional sparse code; climbing-fiber error signal modifies which parallel-fiber inputs each Purkinje cell listens to. The result is supervised learning of context→prediction mappings. Foundational computational theory of cerebellum. Substrate analogue: the substrate's whole anticipation pipeline.

concepts.name: forward_model
concepts.definition: An internal model that predicts the sensory consequence of an action BEFORE it occurs. Cerebellum implements forward models for motor + cognitive functions. Substrate analogue: the substrate's anticipation handler computing ∂²F (predicted state change).

concepts.name: inverse_model
concepts.definition: Maps desired outcome → required action. Cerebellum has both forward + inverse models in parallel circuits. Substrate analogue: motor schema selection given goal state.

concepts.name: temporal_difference_prediction
concepts.definition: The cerebellum predicts outcomes at multiple timescales simultaneously. Different Purkinje cell populations encode different prediction horizons. Substrate analogue: ∂²F as second-order temporal difference.

concepts.name: cerebro_cerebellar_loop
concepts.definition: Every cortical area projects to cerebellum (via pons) and receives back from cerebellum (via thalamus). Not just motor — prefrontal, parietal, temporal, all loop through cerebellum. The 'universal predictor' view.

concepts.name: modular_organization
concepts.definition: Cerebellum is divided into ~hundred microzones, each receiving its own climbing-fiber input + each handling one prediction. Each microzone is an independent learner. Substrate analogue: one anticipation Mt per concept domain.

concepts.name: vermis_versus_hemisphere
concepts.definition: Medial vermis handles posture + balance + emotion; lateral hemispheres handle limb coordination + cognition. Anatomical specialisation by function. Substrate analogue: different anticipation handlers for different drive domains.

concepts.name: motor_timing
concepts.definition: Cerebellum learns precise temporal sequences. Eye-blink conditioning is the classic example: pair tone + airpuff at exactly 250ms; learn to blink at 250ms. Lesion abolishes the learned timing. Substrate analogue: streak detection's exact-K timing.

concepts.name: coordination
concepts.definition: Cerebellum synchronizes multi-muscle, multi-joint movements. Lesion → ataxia (jerky uncoordinated movement). Substrate analogue: cross-Mt coherence enforcement.

concepts.name: motor_learning
concepts.definition: Cerebellum drives skill acquisition. The smooth ramp from clumsy to expert reaching/typing/playing-piano happens in cerebellum. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec refinement through error-driven updates.

concepts.name: cognitive_prediction
concepts.definition: Cerebellum also predicts cognitive outcomes — what the next word will be, what someone is about to say, what consequence will follow. Schmahmann's cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome documents this. Substrate analogue: anticipation across non-motor Mts.

concepts.name: language_prediction
concepts.definition: Cerebellum predicts upcoming words in sentences; lesion impairs verb generation. Subverbal motor simulation. Substrate analogue: anticipation in the substrate's lexical access cortex.

rules.name: cerebellum_predicts_consequence
rules.head: an action is initiated
rules.body: the cerebellum predicts its sensory consequence in parallel. If prediction matches actual, no error; if mismatch, climbing-fiber fires and learns. Substrate's anticipation handler is this mechanism.

rules.name: climbing_fiber_carries_error
rules.head: the actual outcome diverges from the cerebellar prediction
rules.body: the inferior olive fires a climbing-fiber spike to the relevant Purkinje cell, triggering LTD at parallel-fiber synapses that contributed to the wrong prediction. Substrate analogue: ΔF as the teaching signal for anticipation weights.

rules.name: sparse_expansion_in_granule_layer
rules.head: low-dimensional mossy-fiber input arrives at granule cell layer
rules.body: granule cells expand it into a high-dimensional sparse code (Marr 1969) that increases the cerebellum's pattern-separation capacity. Substrate analogue: the substrate's feature_invention process — expanding existing features into more discriminative ones.

rules.name: microzones_are_independent_learners
rules.head: cerebellum is functionally divided into ~hundred microzones
rules.body: each receives its own error signal + makes its own prediction independently. Failures in one microzone don't propagate to others. Substrate analogue: per-Mt anticipation isolation.

rules.name: cerebellum_is_universal_predictor
rules.head: any cortical region engaged in any task
rules.body: loops through cerebellum to receive prediction support. Not motor-specific. Substrate analogue: anticipation handler should run for every Mt, not just motor ones.
